title: Unit 6: Ecology
description: Comprehensive questions covering Grade 9 Biology Unit 6

questions.question: What is ecology?
options: The study of the interactions among organisms and with their environment
The study of rocks and minerals
The study of the solar system
questions.correctAnswer: The study of the interactions among organisms and with their environment
questions.explanation: Ecology is the branch of biology that deals with the study of the interactions among organisms and with their environment.

questions.question: What do we call scientists who study ecology?
questions.correctAnswer: Ecologists
questions.explanation: Scientists who study ecology are called ecologists.

questions.question: What is a habitat?
options: The job an organism does in its environment
The place where a living thing lives
The role of decomposers in an ecosystem
questions.correctAnswer: The place where a living thing lives
questions.explanation: Each type of living thing in an ecosystem has a place in which it lives, known as its habitat.

questions.question: What is a niche?
options: The place where an organism lives
A group of the same species in an area
The combination of the job an organism does and the place in which it lives
A non-living component of the ecosystem
questions.correctAnswer: The combination of the job an organism does and the place in which it lives
questions.explanation: The combination of the job an organism does and the place in which it lives is called its niche.

questions.question: What is a population?
options: All the different species in an area
A group of interbreeding organisms that are members of the same species living in the same area at the same time
The non-living components of an ecosystem
questions.correctAnswer: A group of interbreeding organisms that are members of the same species living in the same area at the same time
questions.explanation: A population is a group of interbreeding organisms that are members of the same species living in the same area at the same time.

questions.question: What is a biological community?
options: A group of the same species in an area
The different species within an area and the interactions within and among these species
The abiotic factors in an environment
A single organism living in a habitat
questions.correctAnswer: The different species within an area and the interactions within and among these species
questions.explanation: A biological community consists of the different species within an area and the interactions within and among these species.

questions.question: What is an ecosystem?
options: The community of organisms in a habitat plus the non-living part of the environment
A major life zone on land
questions.correctAnswer: The community of organisms in a habitat plus the non-living part of the environment
questions.explanation: The community of organisms in a habitat, plus the non-living part of the environment, makes up an ecosystem.

questions.question: What is the biosphere?
options: The part of Earth's surface that contains living organisms
A community of organisms in water
The soil layer of the Earth
questions.correctAnswer: The part of Earth's surface that contains living organisms
questions.explanation: The whole part of the Earth's surface which contains living organisms is called the biosphere.

questions.question: What are abiotic factors?
options: The living components of an ecosystem
The non-living components of an ecosystem that influence the distribution of organisms
questions.correctAnswer: The non-living components of an ecosystem that influence the distribution of organisms
questions.explanation: Abiotic factors are non-living components of the ecosystem that influence the distributions of organisms in their environment.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an abiotic factor?
questions.correctAnswer: Temperature
questions.explanation: Temperature is an abiotic factor because it is a non-living component that influences organism distribution.

questions.question: What are biotic factors?
options: The non-living components of an ecosystem
The living components of an ecosystem that influence the distribution of organisms
questions.correctAnswer: The living components of an ecosystem that influence the distribution of organisms
questions.explanation: Biotic factors are the living components of the ecosystem that influence the distributions of organisms in their environment.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a biotic factor?
questions.correctAnswer: Predators
questions.explanation: Predators are biotic factors because they are living components of the ecosystem.

questions.question: Which organisms are known as producers?
options: Bacteria and fungi that break down dead matter
Plants and algae that trap sunlight energy to make their own food
Organisms that kill and eat prey
questions.correctAnswer: Plants and algae that trap sunlight energy to make their own food
questions.explanation: Plants and algae trap the energy in sunlight and produce their own food, so they are known as producers.

questions.question: Which organisms are known as consumers?
options: Animals since they cannot make their own food and must obtain it from producers or other consumers
questions.correctAnswer: Animals since they cannot make their own food and must obtain it from producers or other consumers
questions.explanation: Animals are consumers since they cannot make their own food and must obtain it from producers or other consumers.

questions.question: Which organisms are known as decomposers?
options: Bacteria and fungi that eat dead plant and animal remains and convert them into reusable substances
questions.correctAnswer: Bacteria and fungi that eat dead plant and animal remains and convert them into reusable substances
questions.explanation: Bacteria and fungi are decomposers that eat dead plant and animal remains and convert them into substances that can be reused.

questions.question: Why is solar energy an important factor for most ecosystems?
options: It powers photosynthesis which captures energy to support the ecosystem
It warms the soil for plant roots
questions.correctAnswer: It powers photosynthesis which captures energy to support the ecosystem
questions.explanation: Solar energy from sunlight, captured by chlorophyll during photosynthesis, powers most ecosystems.

questions.question: What happens to most organisms at temperatures above 45°C (113°F)?
questions.correctAnswer: Their enzymes are destroyed
questions.explanation: Temperatures above 45°C (113°F) destroy the enzymes of most organisms.

questions.question: What is the primary threat for terrestrial organisms regarding water?
options: Too much water flooding their habitat
questions.correctAnswer: Drying out in the air
questions.explanation: For terrestrial organisms, the primary threat is drying out in the air.

questions.question: Which abiotic factor is especially important for aquatic organisms but not terrestrial ones?
questions.correctAnswer: Oxygen dissolved in water
questions.explanation: While terrestrial organisms have plentiful oxygen from the air, aquatic organisms depend on oxygen dissolved in water.

questions.question: What is the correct order of ecological levels from smallest to largest?
questions.correctAnswer: Organism, population, community, ecosystem, biosphere
questions.explanation: Ecologists have organized the living world into levels: organism, population, community, ecosystem, and biosphere.

questions.question: How do young tadpoles and adult frogs reduce competition for food within their population?
options: They live in different habitats entirely
Tadpoles eat algae and adult frogs eat insects, so they have different diets
Tadpoles eat insects and adult frogs eat algae
They hunt at different times of day
questions.correctAnswer: Tadpoles eat algae and adult frogs eat insects, so they have different diets
questions.explanation: Tadpoles eat algae and adult frogs eat insects; therefore, they are not competing with each other for food.

questions.question: What is a quadrat used for in ecology?
options: Sampling populations of immobile or slow-moving organisms
questions.correctAnswer: Sampling populations of immobile or slow-moving organisms
questions.explanation: A quadrat is used to sample populations to determine their size and density for immobile organisms such as plants or small and slow-moving organisms.

questions.question: What are the two major types of ecosystems?
questions.correctAnswer: Terrestrial and aquatic
questions.explanation: There are two major kinds of ecosystems — terrestrial (on land) and aquatic (in water).

questions.question: What is a biome?
options: A small habitat within a forest
A major terrestrial or aquatic life zone characterized by vegetation type and physical environment
The non-living components of an ecosystem
questions.correctAnswer: A major terrestrial or aquatic life zone characterized by vegetation type and physical environment
questions.explanation: A biome is a major terrestrial or aquatic life zone characterized by vegetation type in terrestrial biomes and the physical environment in aquatic biomes.

questions.question: What is the typical annual rainfall in tropical rain forests?
questions.correctAnswer: 130 to 200 centimetres
questions.explanation: Tropical rain forests receive annual rainfall of 130 to 200 centimetres.

questions.question: What is the average temperature in a tropical rain forest?
questions.explanation: Tropical rain forests have an average temperature of 25°C (77°F) with little variation.

questions.question: Which biome has the highest animal diversity?
questions.correctAnswer: Tropical rain forest
questions.explanation: Animal diversity is higher in tropical forests than in any other terrestrial biome.

questions.question: What is a desert?
options: A biome with abundant rainfall year-round
A biome that receives an average of less than 10 centimetres of rain per year
questions.correctAnswer: A biome that receives an average of less than 10 centimetres of rain per year
questions.explanation: Deserts receive an average of less than 10 centimetres of rain per year.

questions.question: What adaptation do desert plants commonly have?
options: Large broad leaves to capture sunlight
Water storage, tolerance of heat, and reduced leaf surface area
Deep roots that require constant moisture
Thin stems that lose water easily
questions.correctAnswer: Water storage, tolerance of heat, and reduced leaf surface area
questions.explanation: Desert plant adaptations include tolerance of heat and desiccation, water storage, and reduced leaf surface area.

questions.question: Which biome has scattered trees, seasonal droughts, and is fire-adapted?
questions.correctAnswer: Savanna
questions.explanation: The savanna biome is characterized by scattered trees, seasonal drought, and fire-adapted plant species.

questions.question: What is the annual precipitation range in savannas?
questions.correctAnswer: 30 to 50 cm per year
questions.explanation: The precipitation in savannas averages 30–50 cm per year.

questions.question: Which animals are common herbivores in African savannas?
options: Giraffes, zebras, elephants, antelopes, and wildebeests
questions.correctAnswer: Giraffes, zebras, elephants, antelopes, and wildebeests
questions.explanation: Herbivores in African savannas include giraffes, zebras, elephants, antelopes, and wildebeests.

questions.question: What are the dominant plants in temperate grasslands?
options: Grasses with roots that extend through thick topsoil
questions.correctAnswer: Grasses with roots that extend through thick topsoil
questions.explanation: Grass roots extend profusely through the thick topsoil in temperate grasslands and help hold it in place.

questions.question: What is another name for boreal forest?
questions.correctAnswer: Taiga or coniferous forest
questions.explanation: The boreal forest is also known as taiga or coniferous forest.

questions.question: What type of trees dominate the boreal forest?
options: Cold-tolerant cone-bearing coniferous trees like pines and spruce
questions.correctAnswer: Cold-tolerant cone-bearing coniferous trees like pines and spruce
questions.explanation: The long cold winters in the boreal forest have led to the predominance of cold-tolerant cone-bearing coniferous plants like pines and spruce.

questions.question: What are the dominant plants in temperate broad-leaf forests?
options: Deciduous trees that drop their leaves before winter
questions.correctAnswer: Deciduous trees that drop their leaves before winter
questions.explanation: The dominant plants in temperate broad-leaf forests are deciduous trees, which drop their leaves before winter.

questions.question: What is permafrost?
options: A permanently frozen layer of soil that restricts plant root growth
A seasonal frost that melts in summer
A layer of ice on lakes
questions.correctAnswer: A permanently frozen layer of soil that restricts plant root growth
questions.explanation: Permafrost is a permanently frozen layer of soil that restricts the growth of plant roots, found in tundra regions.

questions.question: What type of vegetation is found in the tundra?
options: Mostly herbaceous plants, mosses, grasses, dwarf shrubs, and lichens
questions.correctAnswer: Mostly herbaceous plants, mosses, grasses, dwarf shrubs, and lichens
questions.explanation: The vegetation of tundra is mostly herbaceous, consisting of mosses, grasses, forbs, dwarf shrubs, trees, and lichens.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of Earth's surface do aquatic biomes occupy?
questions.explanation: Aquatic biomes occupy roughly 75% of Earth's surface.

questions.question: What is the typical salt concentration of freshwater biomes?
questions.correctAnswer: Less than 1%
questions.explanation: Freshwater biomes typically have salt concentrations of less than 1%.

questions.question: What is the typical salt concentration of marine biomes?
questions.correctAnswer: Around 3%
questions.explanation: The salt concentrations of marine biomes are generally around 3%.

questions.question: What are wetlands?
options: Deep bodies of water like oceans
Environments where the soil is permanently or periodically saturated with water
Areas with no water at all
questions.correctAnswer: Environments where the soil is permanently or periodically saturated with water
questions.explanation: Wetlands are environments in which the soil is either permanently or periodically saturated with water.

questions.question: What is an estuary?
options: A transition area between river and sea where salt and fresh water mix
questions.correctAnswer: A transition area between river and sea where salt and fresh water mix
questions.explanation: An estuary is a transition area between river and sea where seawater and freshwater mix.

questions.question: What is ecological succession?
options: The changes in the composition of communities after a disturbance, where species are gradually replaced by others
The movement of nutrients through a food web
questions.correctAnswer: The changes in the composition of communities after a disturbance, where species are gradually replaced by others
questions.explanation: Ecological succession is the process whereby species colonize a disturbed area and are gradually replaced by other species.

questions.question: What is primary succession?
options: Succession that begins in a virtually lifeless area with no soil
Succession after a disturbance that removes most but not all organisms
The migration of animals to new areas
questions.correctAnswer: Succession that begins in a virtually lifeless area with no soil
questions.explanation: Primary succession begins in a virtually lifeless area, such as on a new volcanic island or on rubble left by a retreating glacier.

questions.question: What are pioneer species?
options: The last species to appear in succession
The first organisms to grow on a new patch of cooled hardened lava or barren land
Large predators at the top of the food chain
questions.correctAnswer: The first organisms to grow on a new patch of cooled hardened lava or barren land
questions.explanation: Pioneer species are the first organisms to grow on a new patch of cooled hardened lava or barren land.

questions.question: What is a climax community?
options: The first species to colonize an area
A stable community that undergoes little or no change
questions.correctAnswer: A stable community that undergoes little or no change
questions.explanation: A climax community is a stable community that undergoes little or no change.

questions.question: What is secondary succession?
options: Succession on bare rock with no soil
The re-colonization of an area after a major disturbance has removed most but not all of the organisms
The first stage of ecological succession
The formation of a new island
questions.correctAnswer: The re-colonization of an area after a major disturbance has removed most but not all of the organisms
questions.explanation: Secondary succession involves the re-colonization of an area after a major disturbance has removed most but not all organisms in a community.

questions.question: What is competition in ecology?
options: An interaction where one organism kills and eats another
An interaction where individuals use a resource that limits the survival and reproduction of both
An interaction where both species benefit
An interaction where one organism lives on or in another
questions.correctAnswer: An interaction where individuals use a resource that limits the survival and reproduction of both
questions.explanation: Competition occurs when individuals of different or same species each use a resource that limits the survival and reproduction of both individuals.

questions.question: What is predation?
options: An interaction where both species benefit
An interaction where one organism, the predator, kills and eats an individual of another species, the prey
An interaction where organisms compete for the same resource
An interaction where one organism lives on a host
questions.correctAnswer: An interaction where one organism, the predator, kills and eats an individual of another species, the prey
questions.explanation: Predation is an interaction in which a predator kills and eats an individual of another species, the prey.

questions.question: What is herbivory?
options: An interaction where a predator kills its prey
An exploitative interaction where an herbivore eats parts of a plant or alga, harming but usually not killing it
A mutualistic relationship between two species
questions.correctAnswer: An exploitative interaction where an herbivore eats parts of a plant or alga, harming but usually not killing it
questions.explanation: Herbivory is an exploitative interaction in which an herbivore eats parts of a plant or alga, harming but usually not killing it.

questions.question: What is parasitism?
options: An interaction where both species benefit
An interaction where one organism, the parasite, derives nourishment from another organism, the host, which is harmed
An interaction where one species kills and eats another
An interaction where neither species is affected
questions.correctAnswer: An interaction where one organism, the parasite, derives nourishment from another organism, the host, which is harmed
questions.explanation: Parasitism is an exploitative interaction in which a parasite derives its nourishment from a host, which is harmed in the process.

questions.question: What is mutualism?
options: An interaction that benefits individuals of both interacting species
An interaction that benefits one species and harms the other
An interaction that harms both species
An interaction that benefits one species and has no effect on the other
questions.correctAnswer: An interaction that benefits individuals of both interacting species
questions.explanation: Mutualism is an interaction that benefits individuals of both of the interacting species.

questions.question: What is commensalism?
options: An interaction where both species benefit
An interaction that benefits individuals of one species but neither harms nor helps the other species
An interaction where one species kills another
An interaction where both species are harmed
questions.correctAnswer: An interaction that benefits individuals of one species but neither harms nor helps the other species
questions.explanation: Commensalism is an interaction that benefits individuals of one species but neither harms nor helps the other species.

questions.question: Which ecological relationship is described as (+/-)?
questions.correctAnswer: Predation
questions.explanation: Predation is a (+/-) interaction where the predator benefits and the prey is harmed.

questions.question: Which ecological relationship is described as (+/+)?
questions.correctAnswer: Mutualism
questions.explanation: Mutualism is a (+/+) interaction where both species benefit.

questions.question: Which ecological relationship is described as (+/0)?
questions.correctAnswer: Commensalism
questions.explanation: Commensalism is a (+/0) interaction where one species benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of mutualism?
options: Cattle egrets feeding on insects flushed by grazing bison
Cellulose digestion by microorganisms in the digestive systems of termites
A tick feeding on a dog
questions.correctAnswer: Cellulose digestion by microorganisms in the digestive systems of termites
questions.explanation: Cellulose digestion by microorganisms in termite guts is a mutualism because both the termite and the microorganisms benefit.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of commensalism?
options: Cattle egrets feeding on insects flushed by grazing herbivores
A tapeworm living in a human intestine
Two lions competing for the same prey
questions.correctAnswer: Cattle egrets feeding on insects flushed by grazing herbivores
questions.explanation: Cattle egrets benefit by feeding on insects flushed by herbivores, and the herbivores are usually not affected.

questions.question: What is the difference between an endoparasite and an ectoparasite?
options: Endoparasites live on the host surface; ectoparasites live inside the host
Endoparasites live inside the host; ectoparasites live on the host's external surface
Endoparasites kill the host; ectoparasites do not harm the host
Endoparasites are plants; ectoparasites are animals
questions.correctAnswer: Endoparasites live inside the host; ectoparasites live on the host's external surface
questions.explanation: Endoparasites like roundworms live and feed inside their host, while ectoparasites like ticks feed while attached to the host's external surface.

questions.question: What is a limiting factor?
options: A factor that helps organisms grow faster
Any biotic or abiotic factor that restricts the existence, numbers, reproduction, or distribution of organisms
A factor that only affects aquatic ecosystems
A factor that only affects terrestrial ecosystems
questions.correctAnswer: Any biotic or abiotic factor that restricts the existence, numbers, reproduction, or distribution of organisms
questions.explanation: A limiting factor is any biotic or abiotic factor that restricts the existence, numbers, reproduction, or distribution of organisms.

questions.question: Which biome in Ethiopia is characterized by high altitude, low temperatures, and unique plants like giant lobelia?
questions.correctAnswer: Afroalpine
questions.explanation: The Afroalpine biome is found at high altitudes in Ethiopia with low temperatures and unique flora such as giant lobelia.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian biome is dominated by large trees like juniper and podocarpus?
questions.correctAnswer: Montane forest
questions.explanation: Montane forests in Ethiopia are dominated by large trees such as juniper and podocarpus.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian biome includes the Awash National Park and is characterized by grasslands with scattered acacia trees?
questions.correctAnswer: Savanna
questions.explanation: The savanna biome in Ethiopia includes areas like Awash National Park with grasslands and scattered acacia trees.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian biome covers the Danakil Depression and has very low rainfall?
questions.correctAnswer: Desert and semi-desert
questions.explanation: The desert and semi-desert biome in Ethiopia includes the Danakil Depression with very low rainfall.

questions.question: Which Ethiopian biome includes Lake Tana and is important for biodiversity and water purification?
questions.correctAnswer: Aquatic and wetlands
questions.explanation: The aquatic and wetlands biome in Ethiopia includes Lake Tana and is important for biodiversity and water purification.
